accuracy.reason: Live gateway, OWASP and retry sources support every critical boundary: verified identity is not authorization, local counters are not a global quota, and timeout is not cancellation. Both diagrams preserve these roles.

evidence.quote: Encrypting a connection alone does not prove that its caller is the gateway.

mechanisms.reason: All cards specify actors, transformations and failure causes: routing and body checks, protected identity, double-spent local allowance, nested attempts and atomic effect ownership.

evidence.quote: Concurrent repeats cannot reserve it twice. Completed repeats return the recorded result.

coherence.reason: Request path and common policy precede identity and quota scope; waiting semantics precede retry ownership, then aggregation combines the established dependencies before final fit.

evidence.quote: Retry attempts and their delays spend the same remaining budget; each attempt does not get a fresh two seconds.

decisions.reason: Costs and limits accompany each choice: service versus gateway responsibility, strict accounting availability cost, optional versus required data, and alternate reachable capacity. Card 8 explains when a single API needs no gateway.

evidence.quote: A single API can enforce its own identity checks, permissions and request limits.

clarity.reason: Definitions introduce edge policy, authentication/authorization, quota scope, deadlines, deduplication, aggregation and headroom before use. Selective identity and arithmetic examples clarify actual failures.

evidence.quote: Sending traffic to both can admit 200. That does not enforce a promised combined allowance of 100.

outcomes.reason: C1-C4: learner traces request/response, service versus replica choice and possible combined product, decrypted HTTP and bounded pre-forward rejection, retaining note-specific validation; cards 1-2 teach each.

C1-C5: learner distinguishes validated Alice identity from note permission, replaces forged Bob claim, requires gateway authentication and verifiable identity, closes/protects bypass and assigns resource check to Notes; card 3 and diagram support all.

C1-C5: learner identifies combined scope and 200 possible admissions, rate/burst versus exact allowance, coordinated accounting and cost, bounded delayed 429 reaction, and unequal work/downstream limits; card 4 teaches all.

C1-C5: learner fits waits/retries into one budget, preserves unknown committed outcome and noncancellation, computes nine attempts and selects one owner, reuses caller/operation ID with shared durable transactional effect/result, rejecting gateway-only and fresh keys; cards 5-6 teach all.

C1-C4: learner explains fewer client calls but backend fan-out/dependencies, chooses explicit within-budget waits, marks optional missing names and fails required Notes absence. Numeric allocation is transparently a policy application of card 7.

C1-C4: learner explains no separate gateway needed for one adequate API, shared-policy justification and extra hop/operations, reachable alternate capacity, and unchanged database/shared-policy/permission failures; card 8 directly supports all.

sourceChecks.claim: Live Azure API-gateway design describes reverse-proxy routing, shared policies and load-balancing capability; diagram correctly leaves application work in service.
Live Azure offloading confirms shared policies, TLS termination and separate backend TLS/certificate validation; bounded pre-forward body rejection is a sound resource limit, not business validation.

Live OWASP microservices and linked identity propagation guidance require separately authenticated service caller, verifiable identity, service-level resource checks and prevention of gateway bypass; encryption alone is insufficient.

Live Azure rate-limit-by-key warns distributed throttling is not completely accurate and provides 429/retry-delay behavior; linked throttling guidance distinguishes quotas. Two independent 100 allowances sum to 200; strict combined accounting requires coordination.

Live AWS timeouts/retries article defines wait limits and explicitly warns that timeout/failure does not mean side effects did not happen; shared deadline budgeting avoids resetting the caller budget.
Live AWS idempotent APIs requires stable caller identifier and ACID token/mutations; AWS timeout article describes multiplicative layer retries and one retry point. Three times three equals nine.
Live Azure aggregation guidance explicitly permits partial results only when missing data is acceptable and failure when required data is absent; dependency waits and response policy remain explicit.

Live Azure gateway routing identifies common failure point, bottleneck and need for load testing. Reachable alternates/headroom are requirements; replicas cannot repair shared rules or missing application permission checks.
